content: Disheveled-associated activator of morphogenesis 1 (DAAM1) is a protein in humans encoded by the DAAM1 gene. Alternative splicing has been observed for this gene, but the complete structure and function of these splice variants remain undetermined. Function The reorganization of the actin cytoskeleton plays a critical role in mediating cell motility, adhesion, cytokinesis, and other functions of the cell cortex. Recent evidence highlights the involvement of formin homology (FH) proteins in these processes. The protein encoded by the DAAM1 gene contains FH domains and belongs to a novel subfamily of FH proteins that are implicated in the regulation of cell polarity. The Wnt/Frizzled (Wnt/Fz) signaling pathway activates the small GTPase Rho, a key regulator of cytoskeletal architecture, to control cell polarity and movement during developmental processes. This activation requires the formation of a Disheveled (Dvl)-Rho complex, which is facilitated by the DAAM1 protein. DAAM1 is thought to function as a scaffolding protein in this assembly, enabling the proper activation of Rho and subsequent cytoskeletal reorganization. Clinical Significance The deletion of a single copy of the DAAM1 gene has been associated with congenital heart defects, underscoring its critical role in normal developmental processes.
